title: Grand Rounds Dossier — Clinical Case Two-Pane
description: A journal-formatted grand-rounds slide dividing patient history from diagnostic imaging in a strict two-column layout, with a numbered differential list and a JAMA-style case header. Built for radiology and internal-medicine rounds where clinical evidence must live beside narrative without competing.
philosophy: This template refuses decoration: every element serves legibility or clinical hierarchy, nothing else. It exists for rooms where a missed finding has consequences — where body-serif type signals the authority of a peer-reviewed case report, a grayscale imaging panel commands undivided attention, and a single muted teal accent directs the eye to the differential without upstaging the image. It rejects brand gradients, rounded UI cards, and anything that telegraphs 'tech startup'; it should feel like a JAMA spread projected on a hospital wall at 6 a.m. rounds.
goodFor: Grand-rounds and case-conference presentations with paired imaging
Radiology or pathology teaching slides requiring image-label clarity
Journal club case discussions in JAMA or NEJM format
Fellowship didactics linking patient history to a single diagnostic image
avoidFor: Statistical-results slides requiring multiple layered data charts
Public-health awareness or patient-facing education decks
Non-clinical academic disciplines with no imaging panel content
Keynote or plenary talks without a discrete patient-case structure
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the opening spread of a JAMA case report projected in a dim hospital conference room at early rounds — spare white ground, the measured authority of scholarly body type, and total compositional restraint. A single muted teal accent threads through the case title, drawing the eye along the vertical rule as if marking an annotation in the margin of a journal. The empty right pane breathes with latent diagnostic weight, implying the imaging evidence deferred until the next slide. Reject any warmth, roundness, gradient, or visual flourish — the mood is clinical gravity and peer-reviewed sobriety, not presentation design.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a vertical hairline rule at the 5-column mark dividing an asymmetric left-narrow / right-wide split; case title, subtitle, and institution byline are set flush-left in cols 1–5, while cols 6–12 hold a near-empty grayscale field that implies a suppressed imaging panel. A thin horizontal rule at the top carries the case identifier and department attribution flush-left, with the presentation date flush-right — no decorative header band. Text hierarchy is enforced by rule lines and weight contrast alone; page identification sits upper-left in reduced small-caps. Bottom margin is tight, leaving the lower quarter of the slide as intentional negative space.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a high-stakes morning report in a dim hospital room — clinical authority with zero aesthetic concession. Left and right panes hold unequal density yet equal visual weight: dense case narrative balances a grayscale imaging panel that demands silence around it. A single restrained accent touches only the differential list numerals, acting as a scalpel not decoration. Avoid softness, rounded corners, or anything reading as consumer UI — mood is peer-reviewed, institutional, exact.

examples.layoutNotes: Strict 12-column grid split at the midpoint; left pane (cols 1–6) stacks a thin rule-line case header, a condensed patient-identification block, and dense body-text narrative, with a numbered differential list anchored below a hairline horizontal separator. Right pane (cols 7–12) runs edge-to-edge bleed with the grayscale imaging panel, its caption confined to a narrow strip at the panel base, flush right. Outer margins held at roughly 5% left and top; no decorative header band — the case-number rule line at column top serves as the sole header element. Page number sits bottom-right, isolated at the document floor.
